Split a combined BAM into host and spike-in BAMs

Source: R/spikein.R
HORIZON_separate_spike_in.Rd

After aligning to a combined host + spike-in genome with HORIZON_run_bowtie2, this function splits the _mapq_filtered.bam into two BAM files by chromosome prefix:

  • <sample_id>_host.bam — host reads (feed to HORIZON_process_bam and downstream)

  • <sample_id>_spikein.bam — spike-in reads (used only for counting in HORIZON_compute_spike_in_factors)

The host BAM is automatically picked up by .latest_bam() and all subsequent pipeline steps without any changes to those functions.

Usage

HORIZON_separate_spike_in(
  sample_sheet,
  sample_id,
  spikein_prefix = "spikein_",
  threads = 4L,
  remove_combined = TRUE,
  force = FALSE
)

Arguments

sample_sheet

Validated sample sheet data.frame.

sample_id

Character. Sample ID to process.

spikein_prefix

Character. Prefix that identifies spike-in chromosomes in the BAM header. Must match the value used in HORIZON_build_combined_index. Default "spikein_".

threads

Integer. Threads for samtools commands. Default 4.

remove_combined

Logical. Remove the combined _mapq_filtered.bam after separation to save disk space. Default TRUE.

force

Logical. If FALSE (default), skip separation when both _host.bam and _spikein.bam already exist. Set TRUE to re-separate and overwrite.

Value

Named list with elements host and spikein giving the paths to the two output BAMs, invisibly.
